notes: WHY per_cell_floor_usd AND campaign_mean_usd ARE TWO DIFFERENT NUMBERS (2026-08-19). campaign_mean_usd (+$599 / +$2,997 / +$30) is the MEAN of a per-regime walk-forward DISTRIBUTION (crisis n=12, trend n=10, recent n=10 x 90-day windows, README.md:27-38), not the PnL of any single cell — and those distributions are heavily right-skewed: crisis's own MEDIAN is +$65 against a +$599 mean, and recent's median is -$644 against a +$30 mean. Applying a family mean as a per-cell bar would therefore FAIL the majority of legitimate cells (over half of crisis, and most of recent, by construction) — an alarm that cries wolf until nobody reads it. So the campaign mean is NOT a per-cell bar, and is not used as one.

per_cell_floor_usd IS the unambiguous per-cell bar: a cell that LOSES MONEY fails, and nothing else does. 0.0 for all three families. It is a floor a legitimate cell can be judged against without knowing the shape of the family distribution: PnL < 0 needs no distributional argument to be bad news. Configurable per family so a future pre-registration can raise a family's bar; raising it is a journal act, not a convenience.

campaign_mean_usd is retained as INFORMATIONAL. A cell whose PnL is >= its per-cell floor but < its family's campaign mean passes, and carries advisory="below_campaign_mean" with the margin. It never affects the verdict. The campaign mean is a GRID-level ruler (a mean over the whole per-regime window set), so the honest comparison against it is a whole-grid aggregation, which this module does not yet do — see V247_RULER.md for what that instrument has to look like (pooled paired-delta MDE ~$875 for a low-coupling mechanism; per-regime MDE $1,043 recent / $1,565 crisis / $4,118 trend).
The numbers are per-FAMILY, not per-version. Do not edit them to make a run pass. V271.md:82 lists the standing baseline under "Never" for files a version may touch.
trade_count_floor 20 is carried over verbatim from omega/eval/v49_gates.py (lowered 50 -> 20 on 2026-04-06 after a 100-cycle zero streak from low signal dispersion).

There is no drawdown floor here on purpose: scripts/run_training.py never writes observability.max_drawdown_usd, so the v49 drawdown_ceiling gate compared 0.0 <= 0.0 and was permanently, vacuously green. The standing gate reports drawdown_ceiling as not_evaluated until a run actually emits the number.
